Generating and visualising Line of Therapy (LOT) cohorts

Source: vignettes/line_of_therapy.Rmd
line_of_therapy.Rmd

Introduction

In oncology and hematology (e.g., Multiple Myeloma), patients often receive complex, multi-agent drug regimens sequentially over time. As patients progress or experience toxicity, treatments are adjusted, forming sequential Lines of Therapy (LOT) (1L,2L,3L,…1\text{L}, 2\text{L}, 3\text{L}, \dots).

The DrugUtilisation package provides two core functions for Line of Therapy analyses in OMOP CDM databases:

  1. generateTherapyLineCohortSet(): Maps overlapping ingredient exposures into combination regimens and constructs sequential therapy line subcohorts.
  2. plotTherapyLineSankey(): Creates an interactive Plotly Sankey diagram illustrating regimen transitions, tail-regimen aggregation ("Other Regimens"), and patient attrition ("End of Follow-Up").

Setting Up Multiple Myeloma Treatment Cohorts

Let’s set up a mock OMOP CDM database containing key Multiple Myeloma (MM) treatment ingredients and a base patient cohort.

  • Proteasome Inhibitors: Bortezomib
  • Immunomodulatory Drugs (IMiDs): Lenalidomide
  • Anti-CD38 Monoclonal Antibodies: Daratumumab
library(DrugUtilisation)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(omopgenerics)
library(plotly)

# Create a mock CDM
cdm <- mockDrugUtilisation(numberIndividual = 300, source = "duckdb")

# Extract observation period window to build realistic test exposures
obs <- cdm$observation_period |>
  collect() |>
  filter(observation_period_start_date + 365 < observation_period_end_date) |>
  head(50)

# 1. Create Base Multiple Myeloma Cohort
base_df <- obs |>
  transmute(
    cohort_definition_id = 1L,
    subject_id = person_id,
    cohort_start_date = observation_period_start_date,
    cohort_end_date = observation_period_end_date
  )

cdm <- insertTable(cdm = cdm, name = "mm_base", table = base_df)
cdm$mm_base <- cdm$mm_base |> newCohortTable()

# 2. Create Sequential Treatment Exposures (1L Bortezomib, 2L Lenalidomide, 3L Daratumumab)
exp1 <- obs |>
  transmute(
    cohort_definition_id = 1L,
    subject_id = person_id,
    cohort_start_date = observation_period_start_date + 10,
    cohort_end_date = observation_period_start_date + 80
  )

exp2 <- obs |>
  transmute(
    cohort_definition_id = 2L,
    subject_id = person_id,
    cohort_start_date = observation_period_start_date + 150,
    cohort_end_date = observation_period_start_date + 220
  )

exp3 <- obs |>
  transmute(
    cohort_definition_id = 3L,
    subject_id = person_id,
    cohort_start_date = observation_period_start_date + 280,
    cohort_end_date = observation_period_start_date + 350
  )

df_exp <- bind_rows(exp1, exp2, exp3)

trt_set <- tibble(
  cohort_definition_id = 1:3,
  cohort_name = c("bortezomib", "lenalidomide", "daratumumab")
)

cdm <- insertTable(cdm = cdm, name = "mm_treatments", table = df_exp)
cdm$mm_treatments <- cdm$mm_treatments |> newCohortTable(cohortSetRef = trt_set)

cohortCount(cdm$mm_treatments)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   cohort_definition_id number_records number_subjects
#>                  <int>          <int>           <int>
#> 1                    1             50              50
#> 2                    2             50              50
#> 3                    3             50              50

Generating Line of Therapy Subcohorts

We call generateTherapyLineCohortSet() to map overlapping exposures into combination regimens and construct sequential lines of therapy.

Key Parameters:

  • cohort: Base patient population cohort table name ("mm_base").
  • treatmentCohortName: Cohort table containing drug exposures ("mm_treatments").
  • gapEra: Treatment interruption threshold (in days, e.g., 60). Gaps longer than gapEra trigger a line transition.
  • maintenanceModalities: Specifies single-agent modalities allowed to continue as maintenance without advancing the line number.
cdm <- generateTherapyLineCohortSet(
  cdm = cdm,
  name = "mm_lot_cohorts",
  cohort = "mm_base",
  treatmentCohortName = "mm_treatments",
  gapEra = 60
)

# Inspect generated LOT cohorts
cdm$mm_lot_cohorts |>
  cohortCount()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   cohort_definition_id number_records number_subjects
#>                  <int>          <int>           <int>
#> 1                    1             50              50
#> 2                    2             50              50

Visualising Treatment Transitions with Sankey Diagrams

To inspect treatment patterns and transitions across therapy lines, plotTherapyLineSankey() generates an interactive Plotly Sankey diagram.

Key Design Features:

  • Top Regimen Coverage (coverageThreshold = 0.80): At each line step, regimens representing the top 80%80\% cumulative volume are displayed individually, while long-tail regimens are grouped into "Other Regimens".
  • End of Follow-Up Stream: Patients who discontinue treatment or exit follow-up transition into "End of Follow-Up".
  • Vertical Column Alignment: Step positions (x/yx/y coordinates) are strictly enforced so that each therapy line forms a distinct vertical column.
# Generate interactive Sankey diagram
p <- plotTherapyLineSankey(
  cohort = cdm$mm_lot_cohorts,
  maxLines = 4,
  coverageThreshold = 0.80
)

p

Summary

  • generateTherapyLineCohortSet() automates the construction of complex, multi-agent therapy lines in OMOP CDM datasets.
  • plotTherapyLineSankey() produces clean, interactive Plotly visualizations suitable for observational research, clinical dashboards, and regulatory submissions.
